problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods with LLM/VLM planners explore each region exhaustively, causing redundant exploration and failures; small unknown patches on the map repeatedly trigger frontiers even when a region is largely explored. There is no principled strategy for terminating exploration of a region early.
motivation: Exploration shows diminishing marginal returns: information gained per step falls as a region is explored (most targets are found in early and stable phases). Deciding when to stop searching a region and move on could improve efficiency, and VLMs' macro-level commonsense perception can judge whether a region is likely to contain the target.
key_idea: Segment the map into geometric regions, estimate each region's exploration rate, and once it passes a threshold ask a VLM whether the target is likely present, marking the region as low priority (terminating its exploration) if not.
insight: Region-level termination gives the gains: adding geometric region segmentation alone raises HM3D SR from 45.3 to 55.2, and VLM perception (including re-perception of found targets) adds a further large jump (55.2 to 64.3). The exploration-rate threshold matters: 0.5 gives SR 59.4/SPL 26.1, 0.9 gives SR 68.1/SPL 25.2, and 0.7 gives the best trade-off (67.8/31.3). A VLM is essential: without VLM SR is 35.1 versus 67.8 with Qwen-vl-max.
method: Region Semantic Map: builds a ConceptGraphs 3D object map from RGB-D and attaches per-region object descriptors to prompts and candidate scoring.

Geometric Predictive Region Segmentation: builds a wall map from height-thresholded point clouds, applies distance transform, local-maxima region centers, watershed segmentation, and merges small regions below threshold alpha into the largest neighbor.

Region-Based Exploration Estimation: computes the visible area via Bresenham line-of-sight within d_max, unions it with the traversable area over time, and computes the region exploration rate r=|E∩R_i|/|R_i|.

VLM Macro-Perception Termination: when r exceeds a threshold (0.7), select key frames by field-of-view coverage of the region and exploration contribution, and ask the VLM for a three-level judgment (high / uncertain / very low probability); very low sets the region to low priority.

Candidate scoring and control: combines the region semantic map with frontier-based exploration (FBE) to score candidates, uses FMM for local actions, and re-perceives detected targets with the VLM to verify them.

setting.backbone: Qwen-vl-max (frozen, complex perception) + quantized Llama-Vision 11B (frozen, simple reasoning); YOLO-World and GLIP detectors
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x640 with pose, 79° HFOV, camera height 0.88 m; 800x800 occupancy map at 0.05 m/cell
setting.action_space: discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN 30°; FMM local planner to frontier/goal points; max 500 steps

numbers_note: Results are on HM3D and MP3D validation sets as described in the paper. The paper does not say 'val-unseen' explicitly. Per-category results are in a figure only.
results: RATE-Nav reaches SR 67.8 / SPL 31.3 on HM3D, beating the strongest zero-shot baselines ImagineNav-Oracle (62.1/31.1) and SG-Nav (54.2/24.1), and SR 50.3 / SPL 20.6 on MP3D versus SG-Nav (40.2/16.1). The ablations show that each module (GPRS, REE, VP) contributes.
limitations: Region segmentation ties VLM output to fixed map regions, so it cannot use general spatial phrases like 'forward' or 'turn right' (limits extension to VLN/ImageNav).
Evaluated only in Habitat simulation; no real-world validation.
Relies on large VLMs (Qwen-vl-max) and hand-tuned thresholds (exploration rate, wall distance, region size).
